Zechariah son of Jehoiada
zek-uh-RAHY-uh suhn uhv je-HOY-uh-duh
noun (proper, priest and martyr)
From Hebrew Zekaryah, "the LORD hath remembered," from zakar, to remember, and the divine name; son of Yehoyada, "the LORD knows."

📖 Biblical Definition

Zechariah the son of Jehoiada was the priest whom the Spirit of God clothed to rebuke Judah for transgressing the commandments of the LORD, and who was murdered at the king's command in the court of the very house of God. His father Jehoiada the priest had preserved the line of David and crowned and counseled king Joash; but when Jehoiada died, Joash hearkened to the princes and forsook the LORD. When Zechariah stood and cried, "Why transgress ye the commandments of the LORD, that ye cannot prosper?" they conspired against him, "and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the LORD" (2 Chron 24:21). It was the blackest ingratitude, for Joash repaid the kindness of Jehoiada by slaying his son. Dying, the priest said, "The LORD look upon it, and require it" (2 Chron 24:22). Our Lord Himself set this murder at the close of the martyred blood of the old covenant: "the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar" (Matt 23:35). This dictionary confesses Zechariah a faithful martyr, whose blood, like Abel's, cried to God and was required of that generation.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The priest, son of Joash's benefactor Jehoiada, who rebuked Judah for forsaking the LORD and was stoned in the temple court at the king's command. Christ named his blood as the close of the martyred prophets of the old covenant.

ZECHARIAH SON OF JEHOIADA, noun. The priest whom the Spirit moved to rebuke Judah, murdered in the temple court by the command of king Joash.

He was the son of Jehoiada, who had preserved David's line and counseled the king, yet was repaid with the blood of his son.

"And when he died, he said, The LORD look upon it, and require it" (2 Chron 24:22).

His witness required of the king repentance, and met instead with murderous ingratitude.

Christ set his blood as the close of the martyred prophets, required of that generation (Matt 23:35).

📖 Key Scripture

2 Chron 24:20 — "And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the LORD, that ye cannot prosper? because ye have forsaken the LORD, he hath also forsaken you."

2 Chron 24:21 — "And they conspired against him, and stoned him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of the house of the LORD."

2 Chron 24:22 — "Thus Joash the king remembered not the kindness which Jehoiada his father had done to him, but slew his son. And when he died, he said, The LORD look upon it, and require it."

Matt 23:35 — "That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Zechariah's martyrdom faces no postmodern redefinition; the principle to recover is that the faithful witness who reproves sin may be silenced by the powerful, yet his blood is required by God.

expand to see more

The murder of Zechariah is a study in the hatred of fallen men for the reproof of God's word. The Spirit clothed the priest to call the nation to repentance, and the answer of king and princes was stones. Joash forgot the kindness of the father and slew the son in the very court where God was worshipped, joining ingratitude to murder and sacrilege.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the certainty of divine justice. The dying prayer — "The LORD look upon it, and require it" — was answered within the year, and our Lord wove this very blood into His indictment of the generation that would crucify Him and murder His apostles. The faithful preacher must reckon that the world may stone him for the truth, and that God Himself keeps the account, requiring innocent blood in His own time.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

His name confesses that the LORD remembers, and his story proves that the LORD remembers innocent blood to require it.

expand to see more

Zekaryah — "the LORD hath remembered," from zakar, to remember, joined to the divine name.

Yehoyada — "the LORD knows," the faithful priest who crowned and counseled Joash.

The murder occurred in the court of the house of the LORD, an aggravated sacrilege.

His dying cry, "require it," appeals to God as the avenger of innocent blood.

Christ cites his blood as the close of the martyred witnesses of the old covenant (Matt 23:35).

Usage

"Zechariah son of Jehoiada rebuked Judah for transgressing the commandments of the LORD."

"They stoned Zechariah son of Jehoiada in the temple court at the commandment of king Joash."

"Our Lord named the blood of Zechariah son of Jehoiada as the close of the martyrs of old."
